title: Syntomic polynomial presentation kernels are locally Koszul-regular
statement: Let $R\to E$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings which is syntomic: it is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], finitely presented [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ the fibre $E\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a local complete intersection over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]; residue fields are as in [def-weil-residue-field]. Let $m\geq0$ and $\beta:P=R[y_1,\ldots,y_m]\twoheadrightarrow E$ be any surjective homomorphism of $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and put $J=\ker\beta$. For every prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset P$ containing $J$, there exist $h\in P\setminus\mathfrak q$, an integer $r\geq0$, and $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in P_h$ such that $$JP_h=(f_1,\ldots,f_r),\qquad H_i(K_\bullet(P_h;f_1,\ldots,f_r))=0\quad(i>0).$$ Here $P_h$ is localization at the powers of $h$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], and the homology vanishing says that the sequence is Koszul-regular [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Equivalently, $J$ is a Koszul-regular ideal, with its meaning given by the displayed local condition. The empty sequence and the zero algebra are allowed; no Noetherian hypothesis on $R$ is imposed.

proof.text: For each prime $\mathfrak s\subset E$, put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak s\cap R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-ring-maps], the given flat map induces a flat local map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to E_{\mathfrak s}$. In the fibre $F=E\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ the map to $\kappa(\mathfrak s)$ has prime kernel $\mathfrak S$. The defining principal cover in [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field] supplies $v\notin\mathfrak S$ with $F_v$ a global complete intersection. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-syntomic-at-prime-relative-global-complete-intersection] with the finite-presentation neighbourhood $E_1=E$. Its three hypotheses are exactly finite presentation of $E$, the local flatness just obtained, and this $v$. It supplies $g_{\mathfrak s}\notin\mathfrak s$ and a specified relative global complete-intersection presentation of $E_{g_{\mathfrak s}}$.

In each chart write $E_{g_{\mathfrak s}}\cong R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(a_1,\ldots,a_c)$ with its specified relative global presentation. By [lem-sfb-relative-global-ci-koszul-regular] the sequence $a_1,\ldots,a_c$ is Koszul-regular. Its ideal is locally Koszul-regular: at every prime containing it take the principal neighbourhood $D(1)$ and the same sequence. Thus each chart has a polynomial presentation with locally Koszul-regular kernel.

The opens $D(g_{\mathfrak s})$ cover $\operatorname{Spec}E$, because each chosen prime belongs to its own open. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact] choose finitely many $g_1,\ldots,g_t$ still covering and generating the unit ideal. The supplied map $\beta$ already makes $E$ a finitely generated $R$-algebra. Apply [lem-sfb-koszul-polynomial-presentation-principal-gluing] to these charts and the presentations of Step 2. Obtain a surjection $\alpha:R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow E$ whose kernel is locally Koszul-regular. If $E=0$, the empty cover satisfies the same hypotheses.

Apply [lem-sfb-koszul-polynomial-presentation-independence] to $\alpha$ and the given $\beta:P\twoheadrightarrow E$. It gives local Koszul regularity of $J=\ker\beta$. For the prime $\mathfrak q$ in the statement, unpack that condition: it supplies $h\notin\mathfrak q$ and $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in P_h$ generating $JP_h$ with all positive Koszul homology zero. These are exactly the asserted witnesses, including $r=0$ when appropriate.
